memory_dump_analysis: - CryptEncrypt() called repeatedly on user files
- CreateRemoteThread() used to inject into explorer.exe
- WinHttpOpen() and WinHttpSendRequest() used to communicate with C2 server exfiltration.attacker-domain.com

example.detection_method: Correlate endpoint detection alerts for suspicious PowerShell encoded commands with unusual process injection activity. Monitor network for encrypted outbound POST requests to rare external domains. Detect unusual file reads of sensitive data followed by mass file encryption and ransom note creation. Use heuristic detection on registry autorun entries and anomalous process creation chains.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1562.001 - Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools

validation.comments: The sample accurately represents a double extortion ransomware scenario where sensitive data is exfiltrated prior to system encryption and ransom note deployment. The scenario description aligns well with the problem nature. The technical data includes realistic network traffic showing encrypted exfiltration over HTTPS, DNS queries to attacker domains, endpoint detection logs with suspicious PowerShell commands and file deletions, ransom note content threatening data publication, file hashes, registry changes for persistence, memory dump analysis showing encryption and C2 communication, and command and control traffic indicating exfiltration commands. Indicators of compromise are clearly listed and correspond to the technical data. The detection method is comprehensive and appropriate for the scenario. Relevant MITRE ATT&CK techniques are correctly identified and cover both exfiltration and encryption phases. Overall, the sample is complete, realistic, and well-documented, providing a strong example of the stated ransomware double extortion problem.
